paper_title: Computer Organization and Architecture (21CSS201T) - Cycle Test 3, Academic Year 2024-25 (ODD) - Part A (10 x 1 = 10 Marks), partial photo

questions.question_text:
Which one of the following keep tracks of the execution of the program?
a) Program counter
b) Memory address register
c) Memory data register
d) Register
questions.answer: a) Program counter — it holds the address of the next instruction to be executed, thereby tracking program execution.

questions.question_text:
When an instruction depends on the result of previous instruction that hazard is termed as
a) Structural hazard
b) Data hazard
c) Control hazard
d) Instructional hazard
questions.answer: b) Data hazard — an instruction needs an operand that a preceding instruction has not yet produced.

questions.question_text:
In pipelining concept, to increase the speed of the memory access, we use
a) Buffers
b) Cache
c) Registers
d) Flipflops
questions.answer: b) Cache — a fast memory that supplies instructions/data in about one clock cycle so pipeline stages are not stalled.

questions.question_text:
The first machine cycle of an instruction is always a
a) memory write
b) fetch
c) IO read
d) Memory read
questions.answer: b) fetch — every instruction begins with the opcode fetch cycle.

questions.question_text:
Time lost as a result of branch instruction is called
a) Branch prediction
b) Branch penalty
c) Static prediction
d) Dynamic penalty
questions.answer: b) Branch penalty — the cycles wasted (stalls/flushed instructions) due to a branch.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is NOT considered as software Parallelism
a) Memory parallelism
b) Task-level parallelism
c) Data parallelism
d) Transaction level parallelism
questions.answer: a) Memory parallelism — it is a hardware-level form of parallelism (e.g. interleaved memory); task, data and transaction-level are software parallelism.

questions.question_text:
Pipelining architectures depicts the
a) SISD (Single instruction single data)
b) SIMD (single instruction multiple data)
c) MISD (multiple instruction single data)
d) MIMD (multiple instruction multiple data)
questions.answer: c) MISD — in Flynn's classification pipelined processors are usually cited as MISD, since several stages each perform a different operation on the same data stream.

questions.question_text: When the processor is executing in Jazelle state, ... [rest of the question and options cut off in the source image; only option a) 32 is visible]
questions.answer: In Jazelle state the ARM processor executes 8-bit Java bytecode instructions (ARM state = 32-bit, Thumb state = 16-bit instructions).
